transcript:
Meeting header
Date: 2025-10-02 14:30 PT
Duration: 41 minutes (approx)
Attendees: Jared (Redwood AE), Anika (Redwood SE), Miles (Redwood CSM), Daniel (Orchard SRE), Mei (Orchard Head of Platform), Lara (Orchard Dir Eng), Tom (Orchard Compliance)

Summary: quick tactical handover after yesterday's degradation window, align on containment vs long term mitigations, agree deploy-safety and canary plan, share required artifacts.

Topics: incident timeline recap, immediate containment and rollback options, canary + circuit breaker config, KV cache priming, observability gaps, compliance/audit logging needs, next steps and owners.

[00:00] Jared: okay, thanks everyone for joining on short notice. we wanted to do a tactical handover after the 10/1 degradation you saw in our hosted endpoints. our goal is to make sure the immediate mitigations are clear and that we have a safe canary plan for the next deploy.

[00:22] Daniel: yeah thanks. um, we had a sustained latency tail starting ~13:10 UTC, it manifested as token generation slowdowns and then a small uptick in error 503s. we saw correlation with a spike in KV cache misses and longer-than-expected gpu swap times.

[00:41] Anika: yeah that's consistent with what our telemetry shows, the fastpath was saturated and more requests were routed to the Dedicate— sorry, Redwood Dedicate node pool with older quant profiles, which widened the latency distribution. some of the model variants used the non-quantized kernel under load which caused p95 to shift.

[01:05] Mei: couple things — we run burst traffic patterns from our nightly job at 12:45, and then ad-hoc user training jobs later. the spike lined up with a retention job we forgot to throttle. not excusing it, but context.

[01:28] Jared: good to know. for containment the options we propose are: immediate sticky-routing to smaller batch sizes for affected routes, enable prefix-KV caching for repeated prompts, and a temporary circuit breaker that fails open to a lighter model variant. that gives time for rollback while preserving throughput.

[01:54] Lara: when you say lighter model variant, do you mean the quantized L1 variant, or a completely different family? we need clarity so our QA can validate output deltas.

[02:10] Anika: it would be a quantized variant of the same family — same topology but q4_0-ish quant profile — so semantics should be close. we will provide a diff deck with example output mismatches, but in our experience most prompt sets stay within acceptable thresholds.

[02:32] Tom: from compliance perspective we need to capture full audit logs for any fallback routing and any model changes. SOC2 requires retention of the routing decision and request IDs. can you confirm how that's surfaced?

[02:50] Miles: we'll share the audit log export format. Redwood Console has per-route tracing and an event that marks fallback policy triggers. we can append those to your audit bucket or S3. we'll note data residency constraints.

[03:10] Daniel: quick question: what's the rollback window for an in-place model rollout versus a Dedicated — I mean a Private deployment? in other words, how fast can we revert?

[03:24] Anika: in hosted rollouts, rollback is near instantaneous if the model variant is still healthy in the pool — it's a control-plane flag. Dedicated pools depend on scheduler state but we typically see 1-3 minutes to re-route; Private on-prem depends on your infra but if you keep the old artifact until canary completes you can flip back quickly. I'll write that up precisely.

[03:48] Daniel: okay good. we also noticed missing spans around the KV cache priming stage in our traces — there's a blind spot where requests show up as backend time and it's hard to attribute to cache cold starts.

[04:05] Anika: that's an observability gap we can patch by adding a short-lived KV cache priming metric and tagging requests that hit the prefix cache. it's a small instrumentation change on our side — short patch.

[04:22] Mei: the team is also worried about token-level cost blowups during retries. if we enable sticky-routing and lower batch sizes, do we have estimates for token cost delta?

[04:36] Jared: yes, our Optimize recommendations show a possible 8-15% cost increase in the short window when batch sizes drop, but that avoids failing requests which is more expensive from customer impact. we'll share the spreadsheet with delta scenarios.

[04:55] Lara: deployment safety — we want a canary that's traffic split 5% for 30 minutes, then 25% for 1 hour, with automatic rollback on p95 degrading beyond threshold. can we automate that?

[05:12] Anika: yes Redwood Console supports rollout policies with metric guards. we'll propose a canary config: 5/30, 25/60, 100, with automatic fallback to previous variant and a manual gate before 100%. also add a manual kill switch for your ops.

[05:35] Daniel: good. for the immediate containment — do you recommend a manual rollback first or enable the circuit breaker to redirect to the quant variant?

[05:47] Jared: we recommend circuit breaker to the quant variant while we validate outputs. rollback is more disruptive for session state and KV cache priming; circuit breaker buys you time without wiping caches.

[06:03] Lara: what's the risk of semantic drift with quant variant? our legal team is picky about hallucination rates changing.

[06:15] Anika: we'll run the diff harness against your canonical prompt set and flag any items above your tolerance. that will be in the validation step of the canary. also we'll surface a small sample of token-level deltas for auditing.

[06:35] Tom: please ensure all these decisions are in writing for compliance audit — fallback, circuit breaker triggers, and the trails for rollback.

[06:47] Miles: noted — we'll produce a containment playbook and add a compliance appendix with audit event examples.

[07:00] Jared: okay i want to call out three immediate deliverables: 1) Anika will draft the canary + rollback checklist; 2) Customer (Daniel) sends example trace slices and 3 request IDs; 3) Jared will send SOC2/KMS note and a short comparison of Dedicated vs Private rollback expectations.

[07:18] Daniel: sounds good. one more operational ask — can Redwood throttle our background job traffic automatically during canary windows?

[07:30] Anika: we can implement request tagging on your side and have Redwood policy-based throttle rules. it's a short config change. we'll include instructions.

[07:45] Mei: timeline check — we want the containment playbook and draft canary by Monday next week. is that realistic?

[07:53] Anika: yes, I'll have first draft by 2025-10-06 EOD.

[08:00] Jared: perfect. any outstanding questions?

[08:05] Lara: not from me. just please call out expected change in p95 and token cost in the doc.

[08:12] Jared: will do. thanks everyone — we'll follow up with artifacts and schedule the canary review for 2025-10-07.

[08:20] Tom: thanks all.

Transcript notes: occasional transcription mismatches: "Dedicate" for "Dedicated", "KV cache" shown sometimes as "K-V cash". crosstalk present at 05:12 and 07:18.

End of transcript.
